item.title: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
Don't think of a bank account as something that has a dollar added to it or subtracted from it ad random. Think of it as a record of transactions, or a closed system of exchanges. Money does not come from nowhere - someone has to be depositing money into those accounts from business entity. This might be a neat use case for Envelope Logistics, if that's a direction you want to take it.

Basically, make sure there's some kind of reasonable path for the consumer to get money. Maybe they get diamonds or processed gold in the mail, or winning lottery tickets, etc.

item.title: Re: Go For Gold! - Cars, Corpses, and Consumption!
item.content:encoded:
I have very mixed feelings about this. The core ideal is fine, but I'm morally obligated to point out that compulsion should be avoided.

The first two logs are good. The third is entirely too wordy and I think breaks the suspension of disbelief - O5 should have more control over itself and realize exactly what is happening - not break down into disorder and infighting.

The description is greatly improved but there's still a massive dangling thread in that 'bank account money' comes out of thin air, which can't really happen with such a computerized banking system we have today. I think there's room for cleverness in handling that can add verisimilitude to what is admittedly a rather wacky article. The asteroid bit is also entirely extraneous and I'm not sure what its purpose is.

The writing is certainly better than the original article, but I think I would still no vote. The logs add a lot but my opinion is soured by the third log. The ending still works as it did in the original article. As a rewrite, I think you're still a bit hamstrung by the original core idea and I'm not sure there's much that can be done to mitigate that without changing the article fundamentally.
